notes:
THE THREE COMMAND FIELDS ARE LOAD-BEARING. internal/ci/workflow_test.go reads this file and .github/workflows/ci.yml and fails if they disagree: every `run:` in ci.yml must be byte-identical to build_command, lint_command or test_command here, all three must appear, and setup-go must pin the `go` directive from go.mod (currently 1.26.0). Changing a command here without editing ci.yml in the same commit breaks the suite.

Conventions: CLAUDE.md at the repo root — house rules, package boundaries, and the standing warning that a green suite is not evidence of correctness here (`go test ./...` passed with 32 review findings live, 8 critical). Record new patterns there. AGENT.md is the shipped operating manual for agents *driving the binary* (product docs, not house style), and docs/design/DESIGN.md (draft v0.5) is the SPEC — neither is a conventions file. The plan phase reads the spec; build iterations read their task slice.

Current work: branch phase-2a-experiment. This branch is the B arm of an A/B. Arm A is git tag archive/phase-2a-attempt-1: the same design doc and the same 32-finding review, run with a harness that never executed the build, lint or test commands it read. Arm B is this branch: identical starting code and identical inputs, with the loop verifying every commit, golangci-lint in the lint command, the race detector in CI, and a consolidate phase before the PR. The branch cap is disabled for this run so the two arms stop for the same reasons. tasks.json points at docs/plans/2026-08-03-phase-2a-remediation.md; docs/plans/2026-08-02-phase-2-boundary-design.md is the rationale, with 2b (boundary) and 2c (distribution) queued after.

Test layout: Go colocates tests with source, so source_dirs and test_dirs are identical. test_single_command uses command substitution — run it through a shell (bash -c), not exec'd directly. internal/canary, internal/e2e and internal/ci are test-only; internal/e2e/boundary_test.go asserts the import-graph rules from CLAUDE.md against the real package graph.

Lint: golangci-lint v2.12.2 IS installed at ~/go/bin/golangci-lint (go install github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.12.2) and .golangci.yml selects the linter set, with a reason recorded for every exclusion. In CI it arrives via golangci/golangci-lint-action@v8, a `uses:` step, because workflow_test constrains every `run:` to a stack command. Plain `gofmt -l .` exits 0 even on unformatted files — hence the `test -z "$(...)"` wrapper.

Other workflows: .github/workflows/hygiene.yml gates tracked files over 512KB, ralph session logs / corpora / .env-shaped paths, and credential-shaped strings (ghp_, sk-ant-, AKIA, PEM headers). Never `git add -f` a .ralph log or a recorded corpus — .gitignore is only consulted for untracked files, so a force-add stays tracked forever and keeps failing CI. .github/workflows/race.yml runs `go test -race -count=1 ./...` separately; it is deliberately not a stack command because the suite is ~11s clean against ~1m41s under the detector, so the fast suite gates the loop and the detector gates the branch.

Runtime: system curl is the execution engine, hard floor curl >= 7.70 for --write-out '%{json}'. Installed here: curl 8.14.1, Go 1.26.0. No database, no services, no .env needed. origin/HEAD is not set on this clone (`git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` returns nothing); origin/main exists and is the PR target.

Verified 2026-08-04 from the repo root: `go build ./...` OK; `go test ./...` all 14 packages ok; the lint command reports 0 issues; the single-file form runs green through `bash -c`.
